info.title: DiCompute API
info.description: Generated from apps/console/app/api-console/content.ts (endpoint list) and packages/protocol/src/index.ts + multi-protocol.ts (request/response schemas, where a shared Zod schema exists) by scripts/generate-openapi.ts. Do not hand-edit this file -- see docs/reference/openapi.md.

servers.description: This deployment's default host (docs/consumer/quickstart.md); a self-hosted deployment's own origin replaces this.

post.summary: Run a chat completion, streaming or not.
post.description: OpenAI-compatible. Accepts the same `messages` array any OpenAI SDK sends. Set `stream: true` for a server-sent-events response identical in shape to OpenAI's own streaming format -- the same client code that works against api.openai.com works here with one base-URL change. #1761: send an optional `Idempotency-Key` header to retry safely -- a dropped connection can't tell you whether the request billed, and this lets a retry find out instead of guessing. Same key + same request body within 24h replays the ORIGINAL response verbatim (tagged `Idempotency-Replayed: true`) and bills nothing a second time; the same key with a different body is rejected (422), and two concurrent requests sharing a key resolve as one success and one 409, never two charges. Scoped to your account, so a key you reuse is never visible to (or replayable by) any other account. Not supported on a streaming request (`stream: true`) -- a partially-delivered SSE stream can't be replayed honestly, so a keyed streaming request is refused (422) rather than silently ignoring the key.

200.description: Run a chat completion, streaming or not. Success. When the request body sets `"stream": true`, the response is `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, not the single JSON document this section's `application/json` schema describes: a sequence of `data: <json>\n\n` frames, each JSON payload shaped like `ChatCompletionChunk` (see `components.schemas.ChatCompletionChunk`), terminated by a literal `data: [DONE]` frame. OpenAPI 3.1 has no vocabulary for "a stream of this shape" -- this is stated in prose rather than modelled as a false single-object response.

default.description: Error. Every non-2xx response from this surface uses this same envelope. `error.type` is one of: `invalid_request_error`, `authentication_error`, `insufficient_quota`, `rate_limit_error`, `server_error`.

post.summary: Score documents against a query with a cross-encoder, most relevant first.
post.description: `documents[].index` in the response is ALWAYS the position the document held in YOUR `documents` array, never the position in the sorted result -- look a scored document back up by that index, not by counting through the response. Omit `top_n` to get every document scored; set it to get only the top N. Set `return_documents: true` to have each result echo its own document text back (otherwise only the index and score are returned). Supports an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, same replay/conflict/body-mismatch contract as `/v1/chat/completions` (see that endpoint's own description).

200.description: Score documents against a query with a cross-encoder, most relevant first.

default.description: Error. See docs/reference/openapi.md for this surface's error envelope.

post.summary: Embed text into a vector, for a model your operator has explicitly configured for it.
post.description: OpenAI-compatible. `model` must be one this deployment has declared `capabilities.embedding: true` for -- GET /openai/v1/models reports that flag per model, same as it reports `capabilities.vision`/`tools`. A model that exists but was never declared embedding-capable (every chat model, in a default deployment) answers `model_not_found` (400) -- this route never silently serves a chat model's output as an "embedding". `input` accepts either a single string or a batch (array of strings, up to 2048 items); a failed upstream call refunds the reservation in full and settles no charge -- the same fail-closed discipline /v1/chat/completions applies. #1761's Idempotency-Key contract carries over unchanged: same key + same body replays the original response and bills nothing a second time.

200.description: Embed text into a vector, for a model your operator has explicitly configured for it.

default.description: Error. See docs/reference/openapi.md for this surface's error envelope.

get.summary: List models this deployment currently serves.
get.description: Public, unauthenticated. Each entry carries its own per-token price under `pricing` (#167) -- there is no separate pricing call to make before you can quote a cost.

200.description: List models this deployment currently serves.

get.description: OpenAI's `retrieve model` call (#246). Several SDKs and gateways pre-fetch a single model before sending a completion; this used to 404 unconditionally. A model id may itself contain `/` (e.g. `meta-llama/Llama-3-8B`) -- both the raw and percent-encoded spelling resolve to the same model.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Matched against apps/api's own wildcard route (`/v1/models/*`), not a single path segment -- see this operation's own description for why.

200.description: Retrieve one model by id.

application/json.description:
No shared, machine-checked schema exists for this body yet (see docs/reference/openapi.md's "deliberately excluded" section). Shape shown here verbatim from apps/console's own API-console reference:

```
{ "id": "string", "object": "model", "created": 0, "owned_by": "dicompute",
  "pricing": { "input_uusd_per_mtok": 0, "output_uusd_per_mtok": 0 } }
```

default.description: Error. See docs/reference/openapi.md for this surface's error envelope.

get.summary: Per-model rates, posted before every request.
get.description: Public, unauthenticated (#167). Per-token input/output rate for every model this deployment serves, plus the minimum per-request charge every settlement floors to -- the same rate `/v1/account/usage` bills against, so a partner reconciling costs never meets a second, competing number.

post.summary: Revoke the key that authenticated this request.
post.description: Possession of the key IS the authorization -- there is no admin capability and no way to revoke a key you don't hold. Use this the moment a key leaks; there is no separate rotation endpoint, so the pattern is revoke, then sign up (or request a new partner key) again.

get.summary: Itemised ledger history for your account, newest first (#147).
get.description: One row per balance movement (reserve/settle/refund/deposit), each settle row naming the model, tokens, and price it was billed on -- straight off the same journal the money path itself writes, so this can never report a number different from what was actually charged. `?limit=` and `?since=` (epoch ms) narrow the window.

200.description: Itemised ledger history for your account, newest first (#147).

get.summary: Your accrued provider earnings balance, unpaid or paid (#832).
get.description: The EARNING side of an account -- what capacity you've served has accrued -- as opposed to `/v1/account/balance` above, which is the SPENDING side. Session-only: a spending key is refused with `session_required`, same as every `/v1/payouts/*` route; mint a session from `/v1/sessions` first. `balance_uusd` is computed by the exact same function `/v1/payouts/status`'s own balance field calls, so the two can never silently disagree. `null` (not `0`) means the earnings store isn't wired on this deploy yet, not that your balance is genuinely zero.

200.description: Your accrued provider earnings balance, unpaid or paid (#832).

post.summary: Estimate token usage for an Anthropic Messages request (#2274).
post.description: Matches the real Anthropic SDK's `client.messages.countTokens(...)` call. `input_tokens` is an ESTIMATE -- the same script-aware chars-based heuristic this deployment's real /v1/messages requests already use to size their reservation, not a claim of exact-tokenizer accuracy no engine here can back up. Stateless: no reservation, no ledger entry, no dispatch to any worker.

get.summary: Look up an OAuth client's public display metadata.
get.description: Public, unauthenticated client-metadata lookup -- what the hosted `/authorize` consent page itself calls before rendering a consent form. `redirect_uri` must exactly match the client's registered value (see #1738's exact-match policy). See docs/reference/http-api.md's OAuth section, "Step 2".

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Checked by exact string equality against this client's registration.

200.description: The client is live and this redirect_uri matches its registration.

default.description: Error -- RFC 6749 §5.2 shape. See docs/reference/http-api.md's "OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps" § Error contract for the full list of `error` values this surface returns.

post.summary: Approve a pending OAuth consent request and mint a single-use authorization code.
post.description: The consent-APPROVAL step, called by the hosted `/authorize` page's own consent form on a signed-in user's behalf (most integrators using the hosted page never call this directly -- see docs/reference/http-api.md's own header on this operation). Requires a signed-in caller (session or key) scoped to `billing:read`. `code_challenge_method` must be `S256` -- `plain` is refused here, before a code is ever minted. Returns a code, never a token (#1738's "no implicit flow").

200.description: A single-use, 5-minute authorization code was minted for this grant.

default.description: Error -- RFC 6749 §5.2 shape. See docs/reference/http-api.md's "OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps" § Error contract for the full list of `error` values this surface returns.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for an access token (PKCE, no client_secret).
post.description: The TOKEN EXCHANGE, called server-to-server by the third-party app's own backend -- never from a browser, and never with a `client_secret` (there is no such field; PKCE alone authenticates this request). The code is single-use with a 5-minute TTL. The response has no `expires_in`/`refresh_token`: the minted credential lives until the user revokes it from `/settings/keys` -- see docs/reference/http-api.md's OAuth section for why this is a documented property, not an omission.

200.description: The code was redeemed. No expires_in/refresh_token -- see this operation's own description.

default.description: Error -- RFC 6749 §5.2 shape. See docs/reference/http-api.md's "OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps" § Error contract for the full list of `error` values this surface returns.
